portfolio.codebook_interaction: Gradients update the two selected codewords to make their directed difference approximate the stopped-gradient target-minus-source displacement. The hinge barrier gives a restoring gradient whenever their distance is below delta. It cannot pull the pair together: the displacement term can move both endpoints, but its distance penalty is nonnegative and minimized by matching the nonzero directed displacement, while the explicit barrier pushes apart below delta. If a_i equals b_i, the displacement has no codebook gradient through the shared entry, but the barrier is at its hinge and cannot split identical selected indices; this is a known limitation and a falsifier if such pairs are common.
portfolio.falsifier: At the frozen probe, any non-finite gradient, no measurable codebook-gradient signal, a loss unchanged after swapping source and target, or exported codes that violate any required usage concentration, L1-to-L2 branching, train-to-test frequency drift, sequence-information, or pair-level ER criterion falsifies the proposal.
portfolio.risk: Nearest-codeword indices are piecewise constant, and rows whose endpoints select the same codeword cannot be separated by this pairwise term. The transition displacement target may also distort codebook geometry or overfit training transitions; the barrier only protects selected distinct pairs and does not guarantee level-0 balance, prefix branching, frequency-drift control, sequence information, or downstream recall.
